done_when: A restarted worker reloads routes for every app it serves, and a recovered turn in a non-default app is processed; a Postgres test covers restart with a non-default app route

findings.body: Removing the default-app filter makes `getAllConversationRoutes()` return other apps' routes, but startup calls settings reconciliation before `app.loadState()` (`apps/core/src/app/bootstrap/startup.ts:197`). When desired state is authoritative, reconciliation deletes every returned route absent from that app's settings (`apps/core/src/config/settings/desired-state-service.ts:382`). A default-app worker restart can therefore delete the non-default route before it reloads, so the recovered turn cannot be processed. Scope that deletion to the reconciled app while allowing the worker to reload the routes it serves.
findings.title: Not done: A restarted worker reloads routes for every app it serves, and a recovered turn in a non-default app is processed

findings.body: The test creates a runtime app and calls `processLiveAdmissionWorkItem()` directly with a mocked queue. It never runs worker startup, reconciliation, the durable claim loop, or an agent turn, so it passes despite the startup route deletion above. Its `tg:route-recovery` JID also does not identify the non-default app; the agent runner derives the app from an `app:<id>:<conversation>` JID and otherwise uses `default` (`apps/core/src/runtime/group-agent-runner.ts:119`). Add a Postgres test through the worker entry point that restarts with a non-default route and observes the recovered turn being processed.
findings.title: Not done: A Postgres worker-restart test for a recovered non-default app turn

why: After a worker restarts, chats in non-default apps lose their routes, so recovered turns for those apps are silently skipped
